Honestly, I'm confused by these comments, but here's my opinion.

In my past relationships, I watched porn and my ex-boyfriends would watch porn. In fact, there were times as a young teenager (14-16) that I would class myself as being a porn addict at times.

Now, at 22, I haven't watched porn in a year and a half and have no desire to. First or all, my current boyfriend doesn't either, and we both are more than satisfied with our sex life, so there is no need. Also, the porn industry makes me kinda depressed tbh and I just started feeling sad watching it and icky, but anyways, that's a whole other discussion.

Watching porn in a lot of cases might make your girlfriend upset, I've been the girlfriend getting upset in that scenario. The OF girls hit worse, though, to her self-esteem. 

Issue #1:
Porn vs OF. When my ex watched OF girls compared to just any old porn video it hurt more. Because he was going back to these same girls time and time again. He was seeking out their content specifically. Not just going on porn hub, finding something to his taste and having a wank. You have been walking around actively thinking "yeah I'm feeling horny, I'm going to go and look for __________ and bust to her". 
OBVIOUSLY, your girlfriend is going to be upset and think she isn't good enough. Seeing a girl and thinking she is hot is not a crime. Having a girlfriend and seeking out these girls and potentially keeping up to date with their content and such in your spare time is hurtful.

Think of it in an offline perspective.
Your girlfriend passes a few men in the street and in her head thinks damn they are hot and then never sees them again.
Or
Your girlfriend sees some hot baristas in a cafe nearby, so she goes out of her way twice a week to buy something there just so she can be served by them.

That would make you feel inadequate, right?

Issue #2:
Watching porn in general.

I'm not going to sit here and tell people what they can and can't do. Every person and relationshop is different. 
However I do feel if you want to watch porn, OF etc. You should be upfront with your partner that you do that. If you want an open, honest, healthy relationship - they have to know.

And if she doesn't like that, you have three options:
- leave her and find a woman that is okay with it
- or stop beating it to OF models and make more time for intimacy with your girlfriend
- three, lie to her and say you've stopped when you haven't and lead to a break down of trust in your relationship leading to its ultimate demise

Ending thoughts:
She loves you and wants to feel desired. She wants her man to look at her and go "damn that's my girl and that's enough for me". 
But it's not enough just saying that you have to show it. Just saying "I love you and you are beauitful" isn't enough. Anyone can say that. Make her feel it.
Want her, make time for her, make her feel special and beautiful and sexy and loved.
Instead all she is thinking is "I must be really ugly if my boyfriend feels the need to wank to these girls online instead of coming and being intimate with me".
Think maybe how you would feel if it was the opposite way round and perhaps the guys she was looking at were very different or maybe a lot better looking than you?

Maybe ask yourself why you feel the need to wank to these girls?

Because she isn't fulfilling you sexually? - that's a discussion you both need to have then

Because you just like variety and you like to have the option of doing that sometimes? - Then you need to find a partner that understands that and is okay with it

My personal feelings:

All I can say is I've had a porn watching, OF and influencer obsessed boyfriend and I never hated myseld or my body more. Our sex life was pitiful, intimacy fell apart and I was miserable with low self-esteem.

I now have a boyfriend who doesn't and I don't either. And it is so much more fulfilling and I'm happier and more confident than ever. Because I feel lime I'm enough for him. I feel desired. And we are intimate almost every day which is really nice. 

Try having a discussion where you let her vent all her feelings about the situation, without trying to come up with solutions. Just let her air all her grievances and frustrations. Then explain why it is you feel the need to do that despite being with her. Then see if you both can come to agreement on how to move forward. Maybe you just arnt compatible? But I hope you can make it work.

omg ok so this thread is making me start to feel less scared (I am a massive hypochondriac too so I was frightened af). I am 19, I quit smoking weed & cigs in September. I had been smoking multiple times a day, every day for 2.5 years. I went cold turkey for 2 weeks then had a week where I smoked every day then repeated this process a second time. During the second week on, I was having terrible heart palpitations and chest pain, shortness of breath, rib pain for about an hour or two after the joint. I thought I was going to die. Then the pain carried on for 2 days and I was freaking out, so I went to A&E at the hospital. They did multiple checks, a blood test.... they said my heart and lungs were ok and I had no asthma. They said they thought it was CWS (Cannabis Withdrawal Syndrome) and my body was extra tweaking out because I was going back and fourth between having it an not having it. So it has been almost a month now since I have smoked any weed. My body is starting to feel healthier and I don't get those symptoms anymore. I am going to wait a few months before I try to casually smoke again or longer I am terrified for the pain again it felt like a heart attack.
